humanEvidence.rationale: Human trials, several in older adults.

studyQuality.rationale: Small randomized trials with some bias risk.

consistency.rationale: Subjective sleep benefit recurs, mainly with low status.

effectSize.rationale: Small subjective improvement.

name: Stress & relaxation
summary: Emerging evidence for stress symptom reduction, often combined with B6.

humanEvidence.rationale: One randomised trial in stressed adults with low blood magnesium, comparing magnesium plus B6 with magnesium alone.

studyQuality.rationale: Post-hoc secondary analysis with no placebo arm.

consistency.rationale: Not addressed by a verified paper in the corpus.

effectSize.rationale: Not addressed by a verified paper in the corpus.

populationRelevance.rationale: Only adults with severe stress and low blood magnesium.

name: Glucose metabolism
summary: Possible small improvements in insulin sensitivity in deficient individuals.

humanEvidence.rationale: Meta-analysis of double-blind placebo-controlled trials in people with or at high risk of diabetes; the abstract gives no trial count.

studyQuality.rationale: Double-blind randomised trials only; the abstract reports no risk-of-bias rating.

consistency.rationale: Glucose measures improved both in people with diabetes and in those at high risk.

effectSize.rationale: Not addressed by a verified paper in the corpus.

populationRelevance.rationale: People with or at high risk of diabetes; magnesium status is not reported in the abstract.

name: Strength & power output
summary: Robust evidence for improved strength, power, and lean mass when combined with resistance training.

humanEvidence.rationale: Extensive RCTs in trained humans.

studyQuality.rationale: Many randomized, placebo-controlled trials.

consistency.rationale: Findings replicate across populations and protocols.

effectSize.rationale: Meaningful strength/power and lean-mass gains.

populationRelevance.rationale: Strongest in training adults; less relevant to the sedentary.

name: Cognitive performance
summary: Emerging evidence for cognitive benefits, strongest under sleep deprivation or in vegetarians.

humanEvidence.rationale: Several human trials, smaller and more recent.

studyQuality.rationale: Mixed designs; some underpowered.

consistency.rationale: Benefit appears mainly under stressors (sleep loss, vegetarian).

effectSize.rationale: Modest and context-dependent.

populationRelevance.rationale: Most relevant to sleep-deprived adults and vegetarians.

name: Recovery
summary: May reduce muscle damage markers and support recovery between sessions.

humanEvidence.rationale: Meta-analysis of 9 randomised placebo-controlled trials.

studyQuality.rationale: Included trials carried a medium risk of bias.

consistency.rationale: High heterogeneity; creatine kinase fell, but lactate dehydrogenase did not change overall.

effectSize.rationale: Lower creatine kinase (weighted mean difference −30.94); no overall change in lactate dehydrogenase.

populationRelevance.rationale: Not addressed by a verified paper in the corpus.

name: Correcting deficiency
summary: Effectively raises serum 25(OH)D in deficient individuals.
relevantPopulation: adults with low vitamin D status

humanEvidence.rationale: Direct human supplementation trials.

studyQuality.rationale: Well-controlled dose-response data.

consistency.rationale: Reliably raises serum 25(OH)D.

effectSize.rationale: Clear biomarker correction; clinical outcomes vary.

populationRelevance.rationale: Directly applicable to deficient adults.

name: Immune support
summary: Mixed evidence; respiratory infection benefit appears largest in deficient people.

humanEvidence.rationale: Large placebo-controlled trial meta-analyses: protection overall in 2017, not statistically significant in the 2025 update.

studyQuality.rationale: Double-blind randomised trials, rated high quality in 2017; the 2025 update found funnel-plot asymmetry.

consistency.rationale: The 2017 analysis found protection with significant heterogeneity; the 2025 update does not.

effectSize.rationale: Odds ratio 0.88 in 2017; 0.94, with a confidence interval including no effect, in 2025.

populationRelevance.rationale: 2017 found most benefit in very deficient people; the 2025 update found no modification by baseline vitamin D status.

name: Cardiovascular support
summary: May lower triglycerides; benefits dose-dependent on EPA/DHA content.

humanEvidence.rationale: Human trials on triglyceride lowering.

studyQuality.rationale: Includes large randomized trials.

consistency.rationale: Triglyceride effect consistent; broader CV outcomes mixed.

effectSize.rationale: Dose-dependent and modest at common doses.

populationRelevance.rationale: Largest in adults with elevated triglycerides.

name: Mood support
summary: Some evidence for depressive symptoms with higher-EPA formulations.

humanEvidence.rationale: 26 double-blind placebo-controlled trials, 2,160 participants.

studyQuality.rationale: Double-blind randomised trials only; the abstract reports no risk-of-bias rating.

consistency.rationale: Benefit only in the EPA-rich subgroups of one meta-analysis (EPA-major P = 0.03); DHA-dominant formulations showed none.

effectSize.rationale: Overall SMD −0.28; −0.50 and −1.03 for EPA-pure and EPA-major formulations at about 1 g/day.

populationRelevance.rationale: Trials in depression; participants are not described further in the abstract.

name: Healthy aging
summary: Associated with favorable markers; causal longevity benefit unproven.

humanEvidence.rationale: 86 randomised trials (162,796 participants) found little or no effect on all-cause mortality (high certainty) and slight reductions in coronary events (low certainty).

studyQuality.rationale: Randomised trials of at least 12 months; 28 of 86 at low summary risk of bias.

consistency.rationale: No mortality benefit across trials, whatever the duration or dose; the coronary reductions are low certainty.

effectSize.rationale: All-cause mortality risk ratio 0.97; coronary heart disease events 0.91 (number needed to treat 167).

populationRelevance.rationale: Adults at varying cardiovascular risk, mainly in high-income countries.

name: Calm focus (with caffeine)
summary: Combined with caffeine, improves attention and reduces jitteriness in several trials.

humanEvidence.rationale: Meta-analysis of randomised trials in healthy people: theanine plus caffeine improved some attention measures against placebo.

studyQuality.rationale: Randomised controlled trials; the abstract reports no risk-of-bias rating.

consistency.rationale: Confidence intervals often cross no effect; the authors note uncertainty in direction and magnitude.

effectSize.rationale: Small to moderate: SMD 0.20 for vigilance accuracy and 0.33 for attention switching.

populationRelevance.rationale: Healthy participants; the authors call for studies in free-living settings.

name: Stress & cortisol
summary: Multiple trials show reduced perceived stress and cortisol over 6-8 weeks.

humanEvidence.rationale: Multiple human RCTs over 6-8 weeks.

studyQuality.rationale: Randomized but mostly small, single-region trials.

consistency.rationale: Stress/cortisol reductions repeat across trials.

effectSize.rationale: Moderate reduction in perceived stress.

name: Sleep quality
summary: Some evidence for improved sleep, often secondary to stress reduction.

humanEvidence.rationale: Five placebo-controlled randomised trials (400 adults) found an effect on overall sleep.

studyQuality.rationale: Randomised placebo-controlled trials; the abstract reports no risk-of-bias rating.

consistency.rationale: Substantial heterogeneity (I² 62%); effects larger in insomnia, at ≥600 mg/day and over ≥8 weeks.

effectSize.rationale: Described by the authors as small but significant (SMD −0.59).

populationRelevance.rationale: Adults 18 and over; the effect was larger in adults diagnosed with insomnia.

name: Blood sugar control
summary: May lower fasting glucose and HbA1c; effect size comparable to some first-line agents in small trials.

humanEvidence.rationale: 46 randomised trials in type 2 diabetes found lower HbA1c and fasting glucose with berberine, alone or added to standard therapy.

studyQuality.rationale: Randomised trials; the abstract reports no risk-of-bias rating, and comparisons mix berberine alone with berberine added to standard therapy.

consistency.rationale: Not addressed by a verified paper in the corpus.

effectSize.rationale: Mean differences: HbA1c −0.73, fasting glucose −0.86, 2-hour glucose −1.26.

populationRelevance.rationale: People with type 2 diabetes, often alongside standard diabetic therapy.

name: Immune / cold duration
summary: Lozenges started early may modestly reduce common-cold duration.

humanEvidence.rationale: Zinc used as treatment may shorten colds (low-certainty evidence); it shows little or no effect on preventing them.

studyQuality.rationale: Most trials were at unclear or high risk of bias in at least one domain; the duration evidence is low certainty.

consistency.rationale: Very high heterogeneity for cold duration in treatment trials (I² 97%).

effectSize.rationale: Colds 2.37 days shorter on average (95% CI 0.53 to 4.21), low certainty.

populationRelevance.rationale: Adults and children; about half the trials used lozenges.

name: Correcting deficiency
summary: Effectively restores zinc status in deficient individuals.

humanEvidence.rationale: Meta-analysis of human randomised trials and observational studies relating zinc intake to serum/plasma zinc.

studyQuality.rationale: Pools randomised trials with observational studies; the abstract reports no quality assessment.

consistency.rationale: High heterogeneity across studies (I² 84.5%).

effectSize.rationale: About 6% higher serum/plasma zinc for each doubling of zinc intake.

populationRelevance.rationale: Adults generally; the abstract reports no analysis of deficient individuals.

name: Correcting deficiency
summary: Reliably corrects B12 deficiency, especially relevant for plant-based diets.

humanEvidence.rationale: 16 human studies (6,098 participants) of oral, sublingual or injected B12, mixing trials with observational studies; 3 small randomised trials compare oral with injected B12.

studyQuality.rationale: The randomised evidence is rated low quality, from 3 trials with 153 participants.

consistency.rationale: Substantial heterogeneity between studies (I² > 80% in most comparisons).

effectSize.rationale: Serum cobalamin +402.6 pg/mL and homocysteine −4.83 µmol/L; no trial reported clinical signs or symptoms.

populationRelevance.rationale: People with B12 deficiency, with comparable effects across age groups and after gastrectomy; vegans using supplements had better B12 status than non-users.
